'''James William Schwartzel''' (born April 23, 1976) is an American politician and businessman from Florida. He is the Member-elect of the [[United States House of Representatives]] for [[Florida's 19th congressional district]]. He will succeed [[Byron Donalds]], who retired to [[2026 Florida gubernatorial election|run for Governor of Florida]].

==Early life and broadcasting career==
Schwartzel was born on April 23, 1976, in [[Naples, Florida]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.legistorm.com/person/bio/543950/James_William_Schwartzel.html|publisher=[[LegiStorm]]|title=Jim Schwartzel}}</ref> He grew up in Naples and attended [[Bishop Verot High School]] in [[Fort Myers, Florida|Fort Myers]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite news|url=https://www.news-press.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/08/18/florida-election-results-2026-congress-house-nomination/91225307007/|newspaper=[[Fort Myers News-Press]]|title=Jim Schwartzel wins Republican primary in U.S. District 19 race|author=Hannon, Mickenzie|date=August 18, 2026}}</ref> After high school, Schwartzel earned a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in business and finance from [[Stetson University]] in 1998.<ref name="auto"/> He worked as an intern for Florida Congressmen [[Connie Mack III]] and [[Porter Gross]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/jim-schwartzel-r-eyes-congress-090310053.html|newspaper=[[Fort Myers News-Press]]|via=[[Yahoo News]]|title=Jim Schwartzel, R, eyes Congress seat in Florida's 19th District|date=October 21, 2026|author=Hannon, Mickenzie}}</ref>

Schwartzel later entered broadcasting, and in 2011, he began running the Sun Broadcasting company, taking over his father's business.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.capecoralbreeze.com/news/local-news/2026/10/22/19th-congressional-district-candidates-share-views/|website=Cape Coral Breeze|title=19th Congressional District candidates share views|author=Mayberg, Nathan|date=October 22, 2026}}</ref> Originally a radio company, he grew the company to having a presence in print media and television as well.<ref name="auto2"/> He is the owner of radio stations [[WFSX-FM]], [[WHEL]] (Trump Country 93.7), and [[WRXK-FM]], and television stations [[WFTX-TV]], [[WXCW]], [[WUVF-LD]], and WLZE.<ref name="auto2"/> Schwartzel also owns Gulshore Life Media, which he acquired in 2018, and ''The Naples Press'' newspaper.<ref name="auto2"/>

Schwartzel is married and has two children.<ref name="auto1"/>

== U.S. House of Representatives ==
=== Elections ===
==== 2026 ====
In 2023, Schwartzel was honored by the First Amendment Foundation as the recipient of the Pete Weitzel Friend of the First Amendment Award, for his efforts to oppose a bill regarding defamation that was proposed in the Florida Legislature.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.floridafaf.org/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=46:faf-names-james-w--schwartzel-the-winner-of-the-2023-pete-weitzel-friend-of-the-first-amendment-award&catid=25:press-release&Itemid=165|publisher=First Amendment Foundation|title=FAF names James W. Schwartzel the winner of the 2023 Pete Weitzel Friend of the First Amendment Award|access-date=November 3, 2026}}</ref> The bill did not pass.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.insideradio.com/free/sun-broadcasting-chief-jim-schwartzel-announces-congressional-bid/article_3e9623a9-bf4a-452c-b497-6b94fe018fbf.html|website=[[Inside Radio]]|title=Sun Broadcasting Chief Jim Schwartzel Announces Congressional Bid.|date=October 13, 2025}}</ref>

In April 2025, Schwartzel launched his campaign as a [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] for the [[United States House of Representatives]] for [[Florida's 19th congressional district]], seeking to succeed [[Byron Donalds]] who entered the gubernatorial race.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://floridapolitics.com/archives/731649-media-mogul-jim-schwartzel-files-to-succeed-byron-donalds-in-congress/|title=Media mogul Jim Schwartzel files to succeed Byron Donalds in Congress|first=Jacob|last=Ogles|date=April 11, 2025|website=[[Florida Politics]]}}</ref> He faced nine others in the Republican primary, including former U.S. Representatives [[Madison Cawthorn]] and [[Chris Collins (New York politician)|Chris Collins]], and [[United States Department of Commerce|U.S. Department of Commerce]] advisor Catalina Lauf, who was endorsed by President [[Donald Trump]].<ref name="auto"/> On August 19, 2026, Schwartzel won the primary with 29.1% of the vote, ahead of Lauf, who finished second with 22.0%.<ref name="auto"/> He faces [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] candidate Victor Arias in the general election.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.naplespress.com/local-news/tradition-change-on-ballot-in-dist-19-congressional-race/article_00da7729-8c99-498e-9a98-fe443cdb5996.html|newspaper=The Naples Press|title=Tradition, change on ballot in Dist. 19|author=Zoldan, Sheldon|date=October 23, 2026}}</ref>

Schwartzel describes himself a "'Trump conservative' who supports limited government, low taxes and strong defense".<ref name="auto"/>

== Controversies ==
During the 2026 Midterms, in the heat of the General elections, independent journalist and political opponent, Alexandra Zakhvatayev, called on US Congress, the FBI, and DOJ to launch an investigation into Jim Schwartzel's media companies for promoting Russian state narratives. Zakhvatayev's exposé outlines extensive research relating to Schwartzel's close ties to Southwest Florida political figures Connie Mack IV, Trey Radel, and Drew Steele, outlining publicly sourced materials of each figure promoting narratives aligned with Russian state interests. <ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-11-03 |title=CALLING ON CONGRESS TO LAUNCH A FEDERAL INVESTIGATION INTO JIM SCHWARTZEL’S MEDIA COMPANIES SPREADING RUSSIAN NARRATIVES |url=https://kyivfreepress.com/2026/11/03/calling-on-congress-to-launch-a-federal-investigation-into-jim-schwartzels-media-companies-spreading-russian-narratives/ |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=Kyiv Free Press |language=en}}</ref>
